name: omap4_mpuss_init
prose: Precondition: runs at init time (__init) after the PRCM and power-domain frameworks are usable; sar_base is NULL or maps SAR RAM. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV with WARN(1) at once when omap_rev() is OMAP4430_REV_ES1_0. Otherwise it fills the per-CPU PM info for CPU 0: when sar_base is non-NULL it sets scu_sar_addr, wkup_sar_addr (an OMAP44xx or OMAP5 offset) and l2x0_sar_addr; looks up "cpu0_pwrdm" (pr_err and -ENODEV if not found); clears its previous power state and previous logic state; and sets its next state to PWRDM_POWER_ON. It does the same for CPU 1 with "cpu1_pwrdm". It then looks up "mpu_pwrdm" into mpuss_pd (pr_err and -ENODEV if not found) and only clears its previous power state and previous logic state (its next state is not set). With sar_base it writes the device-type flag (1 unless a GP device) to the scratchpad and calls save_l2x0_context(). On OMAP44xx it installs finish_suspend, resume, scu_prepare and hotplug_restart in omap_pm_ops and sets cpu_context_offset for OMAP4; on OMAP5 or DRA7 it sets cpu_context_offset for OMAP54xx and calls enable_mercury_retention_mode(); on OMAP446x it additionally sets hotplug_restart to omap4460_secondary_startup. It returns 0. On any -ENODEV return the changes already made stay in place.
note: checked omap-mpuss-lowpower.c:365-446. Reviewer round 2 is right (the mpu power domain is only cleared, never set ON); round 15 concerned the formal contract, now removed.

name: _shutdown
prose: Precondition: oh points to a valid struct omap_hwmod. Postcondition: if _are_all_hardreset_lines_asserted(oh) it returns 0 without changing anything. If oh->_state is neither idle nor enabled it warns and returns -EINVAL with no other change. If the class has a pre_shutdown hook it remembers the state, calls _enable(oh) when the state is idle, calls the hook, and if the hook returns non-zero it calls _idle(oh) when the previous state was idle and returns that error. If the class has a sysc it calls _enable(oh) first when the state is idle and then _shutdown_sysc(oh). Then, if the state is now enabled, it removes the MPU initiator dependency, releases the CPU idle poll hold with cpu_idle_poll_ctrl(false) when HWMOD_BLOCK_WFI is set, calls soc_ops.disable_module if present, disables the clocks, and, if oh->clkdm is set, calls clkdm_hwmod_disable. It then asserts every hardreset line in oh->rst_lines, sets oh->_state to _HWMOD_STATE_DISABLED (after the assertions, not before) and returns 0.
note: checked omap_hwmod.c:2023-2074. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: the assert loop (2071-2072) comes before oh->_state = _HWMOD_STATE_DISABLED (2074). Reviewer round 1 (early return 0 when all hardreset lines are asserted) is right and already in the prose.

name: dns323_identify_rev
prose: Precondition: runs at init (__init); the Orion5x PCIe ID registers and the ETH SMI register at ORION5X_ETH_VIRT_BASE + 0x2004 are accessible. Postcondition: returns DNS323_REV_A1 at once when orion5x_pcie_id reports dev == MV88F5181_DEV_ID. Otherwise it reads the SMI register up to 1000 times waiting for SMI_BUSY to clear and, if it is still busy, warns and returns DNS323_REV_B1 without writing anything. If not busy, it writes an SMI read command for PHY address 8, register 3 to the SMI register, then reads the register up to 1000 times waiting for SMI_READ_VALID and returns DNS323_REV_B1 with a warning if it never appears. Otherwise it examines the PHY ID (reg & 0xfff0): 0x0cc0 gives DNS323_REV_B1, 0x0e10 gives DNS323_REV_C1, and any other value warns and gives DNS323_REV_B1. No memory is allocated and no lock is taken.
note: checked dns323-setup.c:547-612. Reviewer round 15 is right (the busy-timeout path returns before the write); round 2 right (the SMI register is also written).

name: rcar_gen2_regulator_quirk
prose: Precondition: runs once as an arch initcall (__init) with the device tree available. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV, having allocated and mapped nothing, if the machine is not renesas,koelsch, lager, porter, stout or gose. Otherwise it walks the nodes matching rcar_gen2_quirk_match: an unavailable node ends the walk (after of_node_put); a node whose 'reg' cannot be read, or whose interrupt specifier cannot be parsed (of_irq_parse_one fails, after dropping the node reference and freeing the entry), is skipped; for each good node it kzallocs a regulator_quirk (on failure it drops the node reference, sets -ENOMEM and goes to the common cleanup), copies the i2c message template, records the node (of_node_get), marks entries with identical interrupt arguments as shared, and appends it to quirk_list. It then ioremaps IRQC_BASE (failure: -ENOMEM and cleanup) and reads the monitor register. If the REGULATOR_IRQ_MASK bit is set (IRQ2 not asserted) it unmaps irqc, empties quirk_list (node references dropped, entries freed) and returns 0 without registering anything. If the bit is clear it registers the i2c bus notifier, leaves irqc mapped and quirk_list holding the parsed entries, and returns 0. The cleanup path used for -ENOMEM empties quirk_list the same way (and irqc was either not mapped or is not unmapped on the ioremap-failure path).
note: checked regulator-quirk-rcar-gen2.c:141-235. Added the break on an unavailable node and the shared marking; the old prose's return paths were right. Contract removed because the function modifies globals and registers a notifier.

name: socfpga_pm_enter
prose: Precondition: state is any suspend_state_t value. Postcondition: for state == PM_SUSPEND_MEM it calls outer_disable(), then cpu_suspend(0, socfpga_pm_suspend) with the return value ignored, then outer_resume(), and returns 0; for any other state it returns -EINVAL and does not touch the outer cache. The suspend callback socfpga_pm_suspend returns -EFAULT without suspending if sdr_ctl_base_addr is zero (that value is discarded here), and otherwise calls the self-refresh function that socfpga_pm_init copied to OCRAM (that pointer is not checked for NULL in this path); it returns 0 in that case. No locks or references are taken.
note: checked pm.c:96-135. Old prose attributed the -EFAULT to a missing OCRAM function; the code returns -EFAULT only for a zero sdr_ctl_base_addr (line 98-99). Contract removed: the function manipulates the outer cache and CPU state.

name: tegra_sleep_cpu
prose: Precondition: tegra_cpu_car_ops is non-NULL; v2p is the virtual-to-physical offset passed by cpu_suspend. Postcondition: if tegra_cpu_car_ops->rail_off_ready is non-NULL and tegra_cpu_rail_off_ready() returns false (WARN_ON fires) it returns -EBUSY without suspending. Otherwise, only when CONFIG_OUTER_CACHE is set, Trusted Foundations firmware is registered and outer_cache.disable is non-NULL, it calls outer_cache.disable(); it then calls the firmware prepare_idle operation with TF_PM_MODE_LP2, setup_mm_for_reboot() and tegra_sleep_cpu_finish(v2p), which is not expected to return; if it does return, BUG() is executed (the final return 0 is unreachable in practice).
note: checked pm.c:139-173. Reviewer round 15 is right: the outer cache disable is conditional on CONFIG_OUTER_CACHE, TF registration and outer_cache.disable. Round 1 (the -EBUSY return) right and in the prose.

name: ve_spc_set_performance
prose: Precondition: cluster is a valid cluster index whose OPP table has been populated (info->opps and info->num_opps); freq is in kHz, the same unit as the OPP entries (no conversion is done here; the caller at spc.c:514 passes rate / 1000). Postcondition: selects req_type and performance register for an A15 or A7 cluster, then finds the OPP index whose freq equals freq exactly; if none matches it returns -EINVAL without taking info->sem. Otherwise it waits for info->sem with down_timeout (TIMEOUT_US) and returns -ETIME (-62) if that times out, with info->cur_rsp_mask untouched. With the semaphore held it reinitialises info->done, sets info->cur_rsp_mask for the request, writes the OPP index to the performance register, waits with ve_spc_waitforcompletion, which gives 0 when the completion arrives with the expected status bit, -EIO if the status lacks it, -ETIMEDOUT (-110) on timeout, or the negative value from an interrupted wait; it then clears info->cur_rsp_mask, releases info->sem and returns that result.
note: checked spc.c:262-346. Reviewer round 15 is right: ETIME is -62 (the old prose said -116). Round 1 (kHz, not Hz) right.

name: tc2_pm_wait_for_powerdown
prose: Precondition: the SCC register block is mapped and the SPC is initialised; cluster < TC2_CLUSTERS (2) and cpu < TC2_MAX_CPUS_PER_CLUSTER (3), otherwise BUG_ON fires. Postcondition: it polls up to TIMEOUT_MSEC / POLL_MSEC = 100 times; in each poll it returns 0 as soon as tc2_core_in_reset(cpu, cluster) or ve_spc_cpu_in_wfi(cpu, cluster) is true, otherwise it sleeps POLL_MSEC (10 ms) with msleep and tries again; after the last poll it returns -ETIMEDOUT (-110). It takes no locks.
note: checked tc2_pm.c:124-152. Contract removed because the function reads hardware registers; the BUG_ON is not a normal return.

name: zynq_early_slcr_init
prose: Precondition: runs early at init (__init) with the device tree available. Postcondition: if no node compatible with "xlnx,zynq-slcr" exists, or of_iomap(np, 0) fails, it prints an error and calls BUG() (does not return normally). Otherwise it stores the mapping in zynq_slcr_base and in np->data, then looks up the syscon regmap into zynq_slcr_regmap. If that lookup fails it prints an error, releases the node reference with of_node_put and returns -ENODEV (zynq_slcr_regmap then holds the error pointer). Otherwise it unlocks the SLCR, updates SLCR_L2C_RAM bits with regmap_update_bits(0x70707 mask, 0x20202) (result ignored), registers the restart handler, prints a message, releases the node reference and returns 0.
note: checked slcr.c:194-232.

name: BUILD_RAC_CACHE_OP(kern_cache_all, nobarrier)
prose: Generated function b15_flush_kern_cache_all(void) (cache-b15-rac.c:104-123). Precondition: the caller does not hold rac_lock; if the RAC_ENABLED bit of b15_rac_flags is set, b15_rac_base and rac_flush_offset are valid. Postcondition: returns nothing and calls v7_flush_kern_cache_all exactly once. If the RAC_SUSPENDED bit is set it calls v7_flush_kern_cache_all directly and returns without taking rac_lock or touching the RAC registers. Otherwise it takes rac_lock (spin_lock), reads the RAC_ENABLED bit into do_flush, and if it is set it disables the RAC and flushes it (saving the CONFIG0 value) before the v7 flush and re-enables it with the saved value afterwards; if it is clear it does no RAC register access (the 'bar' argument nobarrier expands to nothing); it releases rac_lock and leaves b15_rac_flags unchanged.
note: checked cache-b15-rac.c:63-123 and the invocation at line 143.

name: aurora_range_end
prose: Precondition: start + 1 and start + 4096 (via PAGE_ALIGN) do not overflow unsigned long; end is any unsigned long. Postcondition: returns end reduced twice: first to start + AURORA_MAX_RANGE_SIZE (1024) if end is larger, then to PAGE_ALIGN(start + 1) (the first page boundary above start) if that is smaller, i.e. the minimum of end, start + 1024 and PAGE_ALIGN(start + 1). It reads no state other than the constants and takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head: the function is aurora_range_end (cache-l2x0.c:1357-1371). Old prose and contract used 1048576; AURORA_MAX_RANGE_SIZE is 1024 (cache-aurora-l2.h:89), so they were wrong. Contract removed (depends on PAGE_SIZE).

name: check_and_switch_context
prose: Precondition: mm is a live mm with a valid pgd and context.id; the function runs on the current CPU (smp_processor_id); tsk is not used. Postcondition: returns nothing. It calls check_vmalloc_seq(mm) and cpu_set_reserved_ttbr0(). If mm->context.id belongs to the current ASID generation and atomic64_xchg of this CPU's active_asids with that ASID returns non-zero, it goes straight to cpu_switch_mm (no lock taken, mm_cpumask not updated). Otherwise it takes cpu_asid_lock with interrupts saved, re-reads the id and, if it is stale, replaces it with new_context(mm, cpu); if this CPU is set in tlb_flush_pending it clears the bit and flushes the branch predictor and TLB locally; it sets this CPU's active_asids to the ASID, sets this CPU in mm_cpumask(mm) and releases the lock restoring the saved interrupt flags. On both paths it finishes with cpu_switch_mm(mm->pgd, mm).
note: checked context.c:237-276. The old prose said the function requires interrupts enabled and always sets mm_cpumask and active_asids under the lock; the fast path (lines 250-253) does neither under the lock, and the lock uses irqsave so no interrupt-state precondition is needed.

name: PerformComparison
prose: Precondition: none; opcode is any 32-bit value and the FPA11 registers may hold any type tags. Postcondition: static function returning 0 or 1. In a CONFIG_FPE_NWFPE_XP build it returns 0, leaving the FPSR condition flags unchanged, when fType[Fn] is not typeSingle, typeDouble or typeExtended, or when Fn is not a NaN and Fm is a non-constant register whose type tag is not one of those three. In a non-XP build there is no return 0: it always returns 1. Operands that are NaN (Fn, or Fm when it is a register; checked before the Fm type test in the XP build) take the unordered path: it sets the V flag, clears N and Z, sets C only if the FPSR AC bit is set, raises the invalid exception only if opcode bit 0x400000 is set, writes the flags and returns 1. Otherwise, if opcode bit 0x200000 is set the sign of Fm is inverted, and the flags are N when Fn < Fm, Z when Fn == Fm and C when Fm < Fn, V clear, written with writeConditionCodes before returning 1. The comparison is done in 80-bit extended precision in an XP build; in a non-XP build it is done in single precision when Fn is single and Fm is a constant or also single, and otherwise in double precision (extended-tagged registers are read as doubles there).
note: checked fpa11_cprt.c:142-358. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: the non-XP path (lines 223-327) has no return 0 at all. Round 2 is right (non-XP compares in Fn's precision and does not handle extended).

name: vfp_double_ftouiz
prose: Precondition: sd is the index of the destination single-precision VFP register, dm the index of the source double-precision register; unused and fpscr are ignored. Postcondition: returns vfp_double_ftoui(sd, unused, dm, FPSCR_ROUND_TOZERO), which stores into register sd the 32-bit unsigned integer obtained by truncating the double in dm toward zero, and returns its exception flags: FPSCR_IDC for a denormal input (a denormal also gives FPSCR_IXC because it is non-zero and below 1, with result 0); FPSCR_IOC alone (replacing IDC) with result 0xffffffff for a NaN, an infinity or a magnitude of at least 2^32 (0 for negative values of that size); for 1 <= |x| < 2^32 the truncated value with FPSCR_IXC if bits were discarded, except that a negative value whose truncation is non-zero gives result 0 with FPSCR_IOC; for 0 < |x| < 1 result 0 with FPSCR_IXC; and zero gives 0 with no flags.
note: checked vfpdouble.c:506-582. Reviewer round 15 is right (a denormal input sets IXC as well as IDC); rounds 1 and 2 (dd versus sd) are wrong: the parameter is sd.

name: sm4_ce_gcm_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs at module init (__init). Postcondition: returns -ENODEV without registering anything when cpu_have_named_feature(PMULL) is false; otherwise it returns the result of crypto_register_aead(&sm4_gcm_alg): 0 with the algorithm registered, or the negative errno from that call.
note: checked sm4-ce-gcm-glue.c:255-261. Contract removed because the function has a registration side effect.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, add, I)
prose: Generated function __ll_sc_atomic_add(int i, atomic_t *v), produced by ATOMIC_OP(add, add, I) inside ATOMIC_OPS (atomic_ll_sc.h:25-40, 84-95). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t. Postcondition: after a prefetch-for-store it runs an ldxr / add / stxr loop on v->counter, repeating while the exclusive store fails, so v->counter becomes its previous value plus i (32-bit wraparound) without losing a concurrent update. It returns nothing and has neither a barrier nor a 'memory' clobber (relaxed). The same ATOMIC_OPS invocation also generates the _return and fetch_ variants, which are separate functions.
note: checked atomic_ll_sc.h:25-40.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, add, I)
prose: Generated function __ll_sc_atomic_add_return(int i, atomic_t *v), produced by ATOMIC_OP_RETURN(, dmb ish, , l, "memory", add, add, I) (atomic_ll_sc.h:42-61, 84-95). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t. Postcondition: it loops ldxr / add / stlxr (release store) until the exclusive store succeeds, then executes dmb ish; the 'memory' clobber is present. v->counter becomes its previous value plus i (32-bit wraparound) and the function returns the new value.
note: checked atomic_ll_sc.h:42-61 and the ATOMIC_OPS expansion at 84-95: the full-ordering variant uses stlxr plus dmb ish.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, add, I)
prose: Generated function __ll_sc_atomic_fetch_add(int i, atomic_t *v), produced by ATOMIC_FETCH_OP(, dmb ish, , l, "memory", add, add, I) (atomic_ll_sc.h:63-82, 84-95). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t. Postcondition: it loops ldxr (old value), add into a second register, stlxr (release store) until the exclusive store succeeds, then executes dmb ish; v->counter becomes old + i (32-bit wraparound) and the function returns the old value.
note: checked atomic_ll_sc.h:63-82.

name: __CMPXCHG_CASE( , , , 64, , , , , L)
prose: Generated function __ll_sc__cmpxchg_case_64(volatile void *ptr, unsigned long old, u64 new) (atomic_ll_sc.h:239-262, invocation at 281). Precondition: ptr points to a naturally aligned u64 that the caller may read and write. Postcondition: it loops ldxr of *ptr; if the loaded value differs from old it leaves the loop without storing; otherwise it executes stxr of new and retries if the store fails. It returns the loaded value: so when *ptr equaled old it is replaced by new and old is returned, otherwise *ptr is unchanged and its current value is returned. This variant has no acquire, release or barrier and no 'memory' clobber.
note: the item name __ll_sc__cmpxchg_case_64 is generated by the __CMPXCHG_CASE macro; checked atomic_ll_sc.h:239-262. The old contract was dropped because it dereferences ptr.

name: __CMPXCHG_CASE(x, , , 64, )
prose: Generated function __lse__cmpxchg_case_64(volatile void *ptr, u64 old, u64 new) (atomic_lse.h:248-266, invocation at 268); the listed name __lse__cmpxchg64 does not exist. Precondition: ptr points to a naturally aligned u64 that the caller may read and write. Postcondition: executes a single CAS instruction with no ordering suffix on *ptr: if the 64-bit value at *ptr equals old it is replaced by new, and in either case the function returns the value that was at *ptr before the operation (the old register is updated with the loaded value). It has no acquire or release semantics and no 'memory' clobber.
note: real generated name checked at atomic_lse.h:248-268.

Precondition: ptr points to a naturally aligned u64 that the caller may read and write. Postcondition: executes a single CASAL instruction on *ptr: if the 64-bit value at *ptr equals old it is replaced by new; in either case the function returns the value that was at *ptr before the operation. The instruction has acquire and release semantics and the asm has a 'memory' clobber.

prose: Generated function __lse__cmpxchg128_mb(volatile u128 *ptr, u128 old, u128 new) (atomic_lse.h:284-308, invocation at 311). Precondition: ptr points to a 16-byte aligned 128-bit region that the caller may read and write. Postcondition: executes CASPAL on the register pairs holding old and new and the memory pair at *ptr: if the 128-bit value at *ptr equals old it is replaced by new; in either case the function returns the 128-bit value that was at *ptr before the operation. The operation has acquire and release semantics and the asm has a 'memory' clobber.

name: __XCHG_CASE(w, sfx, name, sz, mb, nop_lse, acq, acq_lse, rel, cl)
prose: Macro definition (cmpxchg.h:21-45) that generates the sixteen static inline functions __xchg_case_<name><sz>(u<sz> x, volatile void *ptr) for sizes 8, 16, 32, 64 and the four orderings (none, acq_, rel_, mb_). Each function atomically stores x at *ptr and returns the value that was there before. The asm is selected at run time by ARM64_LSE_ATOMIC_INSN: with LL/SC it prefetches and loops ldxr (ldaxr for acq) and stxr (stlxr for rel and mb_) until the exclusive store succeeds, with a trailing dmb ish for mb_; with LSE it uses one SWP instruction (swpa, swpl or swpal as the ordering requires) padded with nops. All variants except the unordered one carry a 'memory' clobber. Precondition: ptr points to an aligned object of the generated size.
note: family of generated functions described through the macro head; checked cmpxchg.h:21-62. The listed wildcard name __xchg_case_* is not a single function.

name: __XCHG_GEN(sfx)
prose: Macro definition (cmpxchg.h:64-83) that generates the four functions __arch_xchg, __arch_xchg_acq, __arch_xchg_rel and __arch_xchg_mb, each of the form unsigned long __arch_xchg<sfx>(unsigned long x, volatile void *ptr, int size). Each function switches on size: for 1, 2, 4 or 8 it returns __xchg_case<sfx>_8/16/32/64(x, ptr), i.e. the previous value of the object after atomically storing x; any other size reaches BUILD_BUG() (a compile-time error when size is a constant) followed by unreachable().
note: family described through the macro head; checked cmpxchg.h:64-88. The listed wildcard name __arch_xchg* is not a single function.

name: __CMPXCHG_CASE(name, sz)
prose: Macro definition (cmpxchg.h:105-112) that generates the sixteen static inline functions __cmpxchg_case_<name><sz>(volatile void *ptr, u<sz> old, u<sz> new) for sizes 8, 16, 32, 64 and the orderings none, acq_, rel_ and mb_. Each simply returns __lse_ll_sc_body(_cmpxchg_case_<name><sz>, ptr, old, new), i.e. it dispatches to the LSE or the LL/SC implementation of the same operation (atomic_lse.h or atomic_ll_sc.h) chosen at run time; that implementation compares *ptr with old, stores new if they are equal, and returns the value that was at *ptr. ptr must point to an aligned object of the generated size.

Each switches on size: for 1, 2, 4 or 8 it returns __cmpxchg_case<sfx>_8/16/32/64(ptr, old, new), the value that was at *ptr (new is stored if it equalled old); any other size reaches BUILD_BUG() followed by unreachable().

name: __CMPWAIT_CASE(w, sfx, sz)
prose: Macro definition (cmpxchg.h:211-229) that generates the four static inline functions __cmpwait_case_8, _16, _32 and _64 of the form void __cmpwait_case_<sz>(volatile void *ptr, unsigned long val). Each executes sevl and wfe (which consumes the local event), then an exclusive load of *ptr; if the loaded value differs from val it returns at once, otherwise it executes a second wfe and returns when an event or the loss of the exclusive monitor wakes the CPU, so it may return spuriously and does not guarantee that *ptr changed. It returns nothing and has no 'memory' clobber.

name: __AARCH64_INSN_FUNCS(b, 0xFC000000, 0x14000000)
prose: Generated function aarch64_insn_get_b_value(void) (static __always_inline u32, produced by __AARCH64_INSN_FUNCS at insn.h:303-312, invocation at 406). Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns the constant 0x14000000; no other effect. The same invocation also generates aarch64_insn_is_b(u32 code).

name: __AARCH64_INSN_FUNCS(ldadd, 0x3F20FC00, 0x38200000)
prose: Generated function aarch64_insn_is_ldadd(u32 code) (static __always_inline bool, produced by __AARCH64_INSN_FUNCS at insn.h:303-312, invocation at 344). Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns true exactly when (code & 0x3F20FC00) == 0x38200000, false otherwise; no other effect (the BUILD_BUG_ON that the value has no bits outside the mask is checked at compile time).
note: checked insn.h:303-312 and 344.

name: __kvm_at
prose: Statement-expression macro (kvm_asm.h:267-285) wrapping an inline asm AT operation with an exception-table fixup; it is not a function definition.
note: macro, not a function.

name: kvm_get_parange
prose: Precondition: none; mmfr0 is any 64-bit value. Postcondition: static inline function returning the 4-bit PARANGE field of mmfr0 (the bits at ID_AA64MMFR0_EL1_PARANGE_SHIFT, extracted as an unsigned field) clamped to kvm_get_parange_max(), which is ID_AA64MMFR0_EL1_PARANGE_52 (6) when kvm_lpa2_is_enabled() (system_supports_lpa2()) is true or CONFIG_ARM64_PA_BITS_52 is set with PAGE_SHIFT == 16, and ID_AA64MMFR0_EL1_PARANGE_48 (5) otherwise. It writes no memory but reads the system capability state through system_supports_lpa2().
note: checked kvm_pgtable.h:31-49. The old prose called the function pure; it depends on the LPA2 capability. Contract removed. Reviewer round 2 (field 5 clamps to 6) is wrong: with max 5 a field of 5 stays 5, with max 6 it stays 5 too.

name: hyp_s1_pgtable_pages
prose: Precondition: none; reads kvm_nvhe_sym(hyp_memory) and hyp_memblock_nr. Postcondition: static inline function returning __hyp_pgtable_total_pages() + __hyp_pgtable_max_pages(SZ_1G >> PAGE_SHIFT). __hyp_pgtable_max_pages(n) sums, for the levels from KVM_PGTABLE_FIRST_LEVEL (-1) to KVM_PGTABLE_LAST_LEVEL (3), i.e. five iterations, the repeated ceiling division n = DIV_ROUND_UP(n, PTRS_PER_PTE); __hyp_pgtable_total_pages() adds that quantity for each hyp_memory region's page count. With 4 KiB pages (PTRS_PER_PTE 512) the 1 GiB term is 512 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 516, so the result is at least 516. It does not modify any state.
note: checked kvm_pkvm.h:81-130 and kvm_pgtable.h:14-15. All three reviewers (514, 515, 2054) are WRONG: the loop runs five levels (-1..3), giving 516 for 4K pages, and the old prose's 514 was also wrong.

name: host_s2_pgtable_pages
prose: Precondition: none; reads kvm_nvhe_sym(hyp_memory) and hyp_memblock_nr. Postcondition: static inline function returning __hyp_pgtable_total_pages() + 16 + __hyp_pgtable_max_pages(SZ_1G >> PAGE_SHIFT), where the 16 extra pages bound concatenated pgds. With 4 KiB pages the 1 GiB term is 516 (five levels, -1 to 3), so the result is at least 532. It does not modify any state.
note: checked kvm_pkvm.h:81-141. Reviewers (530, 531, 2070) are all WRONG for the same reason as hyp_s1_pgtable_pages: five levels give 516 for the 1 GiB term.
